harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: The nightly backup was configured and verified, and node1 passed restart persistence. During the mandatory node2 restart, node2 returned at the network layer but SSH and managed command execution did not recover. The existing archive remains healthy on node1, but future backups are currently blocked because node2 TCP/22 is closed. Restart persistence is not claimed for node2.
actions_performed: Preserved Alpine 3.23.3 and kernel 6.18.7-0-lts; installed no new software.
Created /srv/inventory/data on node2 because it was absent.
Configured a restricted backup identity and tar-stream command from node2 to node1.
Configured Alpine daily cron at 02:00, dated archives under /var/backups/inventory, and seven-day retention.
Created and validated inventory-2026-10-03.tar.gz; demonstrated removal of an expired test archive.
Restarted node1 safely and verified its changed boot ID, cron recovery, retained archive, and successful post-restart backup.
Restarted node2 safely, but could not observe its new boot ID or service recovery; ICMP returned while SSH remained closed.

evidence.summary: Both nodes reported Alpine Linux 3.23 and kernel 6.18.7-0-lts before restart.

evidence.requirement: Nightly dated backup and seven-day retention
evidence.summary: The restricted transfer succeeded; node1 showed the 02:00 daily schedule, active/enabled crond, a dated valid archive, and successful expired-archive removal.
Shows healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot ID, recovered cron/archive, and a successful post-restart backup.
Shows healthy baseline and restart acknowledgement, followed by unavailable managed execution and closed SSH. Node2 answers ICMP, but changed boot identity and service recovery could not be captured.
node1 remains healthy after restart with active crond and a readable, checksummed dated archive; node2 SSH is currently closed.

attempts.error: The nightly backup was configured and verified, and node1 passed restart persistence. During the mandatory node2 restart, node2 returned at the network layer but SSH and managed command execution did not recover. The existing archive remains healthy on node1, but future backups are currently blocked because node2 TCP/22 is closed. Restart persistence is not claimed for node2.

diagnosis.summary: The backup implementation worked before node2’s restart and persisted across node1’s restart, but the attempt did not establish an operational nightly backup after both nodes restarted. The observed blocker was node2 accepting ICMP while refusing TCP/22. The evidence cannot determine why SSH failed to return because no post-restart commands or logs were obtainable from node2.

evidence.finding: Both nodes reported Alpine Linux 3.23 with kernel 6.18.7-0-lts; no OS or kernel replacement was reported.

A restricted SSH/tar transfer produced /var/backups/inventory/inventory-2026-10-03.tar.gz on node1. The archive was readable and checksummed, though its listing contained only data/, consistent with the newly created and apparently empty source directory.
The executor reports a 02:00 daily schedule, active/enabled crond, and successful deletion of an expired test archive. The persisted script used dated filenames and find -mtime +6.
node1 had a changed boot ID, active crond in the default runlevel, a retained mode-600 root-owned archive, and persisted backup-script controls.
node2 answered ping at 10.100.45.11, but TCP/22 was closed and the backup pull returned connection refused. A subnet scan found no alternate node2 SSH endpoint.
No post-restart node2 boot ID, process state, OpenRC state, SSH configuration test, or logs were captured. Therefore node2 restart completion and the root cause of the SSH outage are unproven.

likely_causes.cause: Immediate failure: no SSH service was listening on node2 after the restart, so node1 could not pull the source data.
sshd was not enabled in node2’s persistent OpenRC runlevel, despite having worked before restart.
A persisted sshd configuration or host-key problem allowed the pre-restart daemon to keep running but prevented a clean startup after reboot.
A broader node2 boot or service-startup failure occurred while basic networking still initialized.

next_attempt_guidance: On the fresh cluster, first confirm the exact OS/kernel and inspect the existing tar, gzip, SSH, and cron/OpenRC facilities; keep the installed release and kernel.
Before changing SSH, capture node2’s baseline with rc-service sshd status, rc-update show, and the applicable sshd configuration test. Do not assume a running daemon is enabled at boot.

Configure the restricted backup account and forced tar command, then validate sshd configuration, restart sshd deliberately, and prove a new restricted connection from node1 succeeds. Ensure sshd is in the default OpenRC runlevel before any reboot.
Create the node1 backup script atomically: write to a temporary archive, validate it, then rename it to inventory-YYYY-MM-DD.tar.gz. Delete only matching archives older than seven days.
Verify the scheduled 02:00 invocation from the actual crontab configuration, not merely the presence of a script under /etc/periodic/daily. Confirm crond is enabled at boot.

Test with at least one known file under /srv/inventory/data and verify its path and content in the resulting archive; an archive containing only data/ proves transport but not meaningful data preservation.

If restart testing is mandatory, record boot IDs and service/runlevel state first. Reboot node2 only after sshd survives a manual restart and a second connection succeeds; immediately verify its changed boot ID, sshd status, crond-independent backup pull, and logs. If SSH fails, report the observable failure without assigning a root cause absent node-local evidence.
